_comment: Beta values for the Blended table (foods-blend.json), built by pipeline/blend/blend_all.py. Per standard: v = values in `keys` order (null = missing), r = [min, max, number of tables] where two or more tables gave the value, d = the definition used, c = caveat ids per nutrient key; s = each definition's values per table, in words.
status: beta: automated, without manual human verification

notice.licence: Derived from the Australian Food Composition Database (© FSANZ) and distributed under the FSANZ Data User Licence Agreement, based on CC BY-SA 3.0 Australia: https://www.foodstandards.gov.au/science-data/monitoringnutrients/afcd/datauserlicenceagreement
notice.limitationOfData: There are limitations associated with food composition databases. Food composition data used in the database or databases may represent an average of the nutrient content of a particular sample of foods and ingredients, determined at a particular time. The nutrient composition of foods and ingredients can vary substantially between batches and brands because of a number of factors, including changes in season, processing practices and ingredient source, and methods of calculation.
notice.australianData: This Work is based on Australian data, and Australian data may not be appropriate for use in other countries.

pointValue: median of the independent tables that publish the value under the same definition
tables: Japan Standard Tables of Food Composition, 8th ed., 2023 supplement (MEXT)

definitions.fibre:bls: Fibre (as BLS gives it (with low-molecular-weight fibre))
definitions.calc:epaDha: EPA + DHA, calculated: (EPA + DHA) (g) x 1000, in mg

blend-beta.text: Blended values are built by automated steps without manual human verification. Each value names the tables and codes it came from; each table's file traces its values to the published source.

borrowed-record.text: Some of these records take their values from another table, or have values nearly identical to another table's, so they count once: they are shown, but not used in the median.

other-definition.text: No table in this blend gives this nutrient for this food under the definition your standard's target uses, so the value uses another definition (named with the value).

one-table.text: Only one table gives this value for this food, so it fills the gap unconfirmed.

two-fold.text: The tables' values differ more than two-fold. The median is shown with the range; check which table suits you.

closest-definition.text: The US target is for total fibre (dietary plus functional fibre); food tables measure fibre by AOAC methods, which capture most of it but not all.

salt-basis-thiamin.text: Combined, as in the earlier USDA and CoFID blend, where a data check showed no salt-basis factor. CoFID says it expresses thiamin as thiamine chloride hydrochloride; the other tables don't say. If they differed, CoFID's values would be about 27% higher (molar masses 337.3 and 265.4).

salt-basis-vitaminB6.text: Combined, as in the earlier USDA and CoFID blend, where a data check showed no salt-basis factor. CoFID says it expresses vitamin B6 as pyridoxine hydrochloride; the other tables don't say. If they differed, CoFID's values would be about 22% higher (molar masses 205.6 and 169.2).

salt-basis-pantothenic.text: Combined, as in the earlier USDA and CoFID blend, where a data check showed no salt-basis factor. CoFID says it expresses pantothenate as calcium D-pantothenate; the other tables don't say. If they differed, CoFID's values would be about 9% higher (238.3 and 219.2 per pantothenate).
